title: DBS CEO Tan Says Market Is Repricing Risks on AI Financing
source_used: The Edge Malaysia (Bloomberg's interview report; Bloomberg page blocked, HTTP 403), cross-read against Fintech News Singapore
key_facts: Tan Su Shan, chief executive of DBS Group Holdings, Southeast Asia's biggest lender, said in a Bloomberg Television interview on Monday 12 Oct 2026 that the market is repricing the risks around investments tied to the AI build-up, which could lead to more discipline in financing.
She said people are now asking for higher returns and looking at deal structures, and called this 'not a bad thing' and 'healthy', to make sure big financial commitments are sustainable.
She said weaker firms may see their credit ratings revised downwards.

DBS has originated about S$25 billion of AI deals this year, often as lead manager on syndicated loans, and has held only a fraction; the financing is mostly for hardware such as semiconductors, memory chips and data centres.

Bloomberg notes that interest rates are rising, global bond yields are at their highest in decades, and market gains are concentrated in a few stocks; PwC estimates Asia's data-centre spending could reach US$8.2 trillion by 2050.
She spoke on the sidelines of a DBS conference on AI and geopolitics, and said conflicts in the Middle East and involving Russia are escalating at a worrying pace.
She said DBS is starting to see results from its own AI projects, including faster fee growth and new accounts, without giving figures.
quote_evidence: "The market has spoken," Tan said in an interview with Bloomberg Television on Monday.
"It's not a bad thing because now, people are asking for higher returns, and people are also looking at structures."
Tan said weaker firms may see their credit ratings revised downwards, though this risk repricing is "healthy" as the market wants to make sure that big financial commitments are sustainable.
why_it_matters_hint: A major Asian lender says the market is now demanding higher returns and closer checks on AI financing, with weaker borrowers facing downgrades.
notes: Bloomberg original blocked (403); read Bloomberg's report on The Edge Malaysia (it cites Bloomberg Television) and the Fintech News Singapore version. The Edge carries Bloomberg's story under the same title as the pool item.
